question.problem:
The formula for the $n$th term of a sequence is $f(n)=1-6n$ for $n\ge 1.$ The recursive formula for this sequence is

$f(n+1)=$
{{field-1}},
$\,f(1)=$
{{field-2}},
$\,n\ge 1.$
question.worked_solution:
The recursive formula for an arithmetic sequence is as follows:

$$
f(n+1)=f(n)+d,\,f(1)=___\,,\,n\ge 1
$$

To complete the formula, we need to work out the first term and common difference. The first two terms are

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =1-6(1)=-5 \\ f(2) & =1-6(2)=-11\end{aligned}
$$

and the common difference is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =f(2)-f(1) \\  & =-11-(-5) \\  & =-11+5 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first term is $f(1)=-5$ and the common difference is $d=-6.$ Therefore, the recursive formula is as follows:

$$
f(n+1)=f(n)-6,\,f(1)=-5,\,n\ge 1
$$
